how_run: npm ci failed (lockfile out of sync with npm 10), so ran npm install and restored package-lock.json with git checkout. Postgres 16.14 via the npm package embedded-postgres@16.14.0-beta.17 (@embedded-postgres/linux-x64) on 127.0.0.1:5433, user/password postgres/postgres, database ottodot, run as the system postgres user (createPostgresUser). cp .env.example .env, npx prisma generate, npm run db:migrate:deploy (2 migrations applied), npm run db:seed, npm run build, npx next start -p 3471. Playwright Chromium with locale en-SG and timezone Asia/Jakarta, light color scheme.
mock_summary: No mocks. Real Postgres plus the app's own seed data (Parent A/B, Child A/A2/B, Seed Child 1-3, Math Trial and Science Trial at SGD 50). To set up the screens I called the app's own HTTP API, which is what the UI calls: Child A2 booked and paid for the last Science seat (Science is now 4/4 and full), Child A2 retried its seeded failed Math booking with a successful payment, then Child B and Seed Child 1 booked and paid for Math (Math is now 3/4, one seat left). Hero shows Parent A with Child A and Math Trial selected. The teacher alt shows the Math roster at 3/4 with a 75% capacity bar. booking.png shows Child A taking Math's last seat through the real UI flow. Math is 4/4 after that capture.
issues: The app uses only a system font stack (-apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Arial). Linux Chromium has none of the first three and would fall back to Liberation Sans, so Roboto from @fontsource/roboto was injected as a local @font-face named 'Roboto'. That is how a device with Roboto installed renders the site; on a Mac the real font would be SF Pro. Monospace booking refs fall back to DejaVu Sans Mono, which is close to Menlo.
Seed data uses placeholder names (Parent A, Child A, Seed Child 1). These are the app's own fixtures and were kept as they are, not replaced with invented names.
Prices are SGD 50 because the app is configured for Singapore (a migration sets the currency to SGD). Class times are shown in WIB because the app does that.
desktop-full.png is the same as desktop-hero.png because the booking page is shorter than 900px at 1440 wide.
The app's own styling puts the 'Booking reference' column's bottom border slightly out of line with the other cells (td.ref-code). This is how it looks in production, not a capture problem.
No external assets are used by the app, so nothing was blocked. There are no images or icon fonts.
package.json requires Node >=24 but ran fine on Node 22.22 (EBADENGINE warning only).
